images.prompt: A Venn diagram showing two overlapping circles labeled A and B. The intersection of A and B is shaded, representing P(A and B). The circle B is also outlined, representing P(B). An arrow points from the intersection to the formula P(A|B) = P(A and B) / P(B), visually explaining that we are looking at the proportion of A within B.

images.prompt: A diagram illustrating Bayes' Theorem. It shows a prior belief (P(H)) as a small circle, then evidence (E) overlapping with H and not-H. The likelihood P(E|H) is shown as the overlap of E within H. The posterior P(H|E) is represented as the proportion of the overlap (E and H) relative to the total area of E, with arrows connecting to the formula components.

images.prompt: A multi-panel diagram illustrating the Central Limit Theorem. The top panel shows a non-normal, skewed population distribution (e.g., exponential). Below it, several smaller panels show histograms of sample means taken from that population, with increasing sample sizes (e.g., n=5, n=15, n=30). As the sample size increases, the histograms of sample means progressively resemble a bell-shaped normal distribution, centered around the population mean.

images.prompt: A flowchart or cycle diagram illustrating conjugate priors. It starts with a "Prior Distribution" (e.g., Beta) feeding into a "Bayes' Theorem" box. Data (e.g., Binomial likelihood) also feeds into the Bayes' Theorem box. The output is a "Posterior Distribution" (e.g., also Beta), which can then become the "Prior Distribution" for the next round of data, forming a loop.
